rows.available: Assuming GI(s) and MN(s), every fixed affine-linear integer system of complexity at most s satisfies the generalized Hardy–Littlewood von Mangoldt asymptotic on convex bodies, with bounded size at the ambient scale. Pairwise nonparallel linear parts give complexity at most t−2 by singleton classes.
rows.needed: The22 integral affine forms epsilon_nu F_nu(r+W_L n)/k_nu on the convex body r+W_L n in X Omega have the fixed-system von Mangoldt asymptotic as X tends to infinity.
rows.derivation: The actual22 homogeneous coefficient vectors are pairwise independent by2085–2097. Dividing each by its nonzero fixed k_nu and substituting the invertible scalar-linear map W_L preserves independence. The earlier CRT makes these affine forms integer-valued with integer coefficients. For each distinguished form, the other21 forms give21 singleton classes, hence complexity at most20. Fix A,catalogue,L,r,W_L and coefficients first. The translated/scaled box is convex and lies in a fixed multiple of the X-scale; GT permits noninjective systems and its size constants here may depend on the fixed data. Apply the theorem separately to each of the finitely many r.
premises: Actual fixed CRT/integrality and positive-box construction2085–2164.
The local-density estimates and removal of higher prime powers are separate.
rows.boundary: No X error uniform in L or arbitrary changing coefficients; the uniform-in-L lower constant is established separately by the local products.

source.publication: Green–Tao, The Möbius function is strongly orthogonal to nilsequences, Annals175(2012),541–566

rows.available: For a fixed Q-rational filtered nilmanifold of dimension m and degree d, every polynomial orbit and real1-bounded Lipschitz test has Möbius correlation bounded by a constant times Q to a fixed power times (1+LipF) times log(N)^(-A), uniformly in the orbit, for each fixed A>0. Constants depend on m,d,A and are ineffective.
rows.needed: MN20 for the fixed nilsequence models entering the complexity20 prime theorem.
rows.derivation: Specialize the published polynomial-nilsequence theorem to linear orbits in the degree20 filtration, as its printed p543 remark explicitly permits. Keep rational Malcev basis, dimension and Lipschitz bounds fixed; split real and imaginary parts for complex tests. The logarithmic saving is arbitrary at fixed complexity and remains ineffective.
premises: Connected simply connected nilmanifold, lattice and fixed rational Malcev basis.
Linear orbit is a polynomial orbit of the chosen degree filtration.
rows.boundary: This is Möbius orthogonality only, not a direct von Mangoldt or Gaussian weight estimate; GT Main Theorem supplies the separate transference step.

source.statement: For a fixed arithmetic progression with coprime residue and modulus, the Mertens product has a positive constant and the prescribed reciprocal-logarithm exponent. In particular the two unit classes modulo4 have exponent1/2; removing finitely many fixed primes changes only the positive constant.

rows.available: For fixed k and reduced residue l, product_{p<=x,p=l mod k}(1-1/p)=C(k,l)(log x)^(-1/phi(k))+O_k((log x)^(-1/phi(k)-1)), with C(k,l)>0. Specialization k=2,l=1 covers all odd primes; adding prime2 changes the constant only.
rows.needed: S(x)=sum_{p<=x}1/p=loglog x+C+O(1/log x), and sum_{p<=x}log(p)/p=log x+O(loglog x).
rows.derivation: At k=2 the theorem gives the odd-prime product c/log x+O(log^-2 x). Its positive leading constant permits logarithms, giving minus log product=loglog x-log c+O(1/log x). The correction sum[-log(1-1/p)-1/p] converges, and its omitted tail is O(sum_{n>x}n^-2)=O(1/x). Include prime2 in the constant. Partial summation gives S(x)log x-integral_2^x S(t)dt/t: the loglog term contributes log x plus a constant, the constant terms cancel up to a constant, and the error contributes O(1)+O(integral_2^x dt/(t log t))=O(loglog x).
premises: x tends to infinity; the bounded initial interval is absorbed in constants.
rows.boundary: This proves the precise error used in the expectation bound; no prime-number-theorem strengthening is assumed.
